title: Memory landscape calibration for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: Produce model-specific memory "landscapes" and runtime heuristics for long-context configurations (32k, 64k+) across representative Llama, Mistral, and Qwen variants to reduce peak GPU residency and fragmentation while preserving latency SLOs and output quality. Scope includes: building a profiling harness to capture layer-wise KV and activation residency over realistic traffic patterns, evaluating slab and span allocator parameters to limit fragmentation for mixed sequence distributions, introducing KV-slice residency heuristics that tie eviction priority to token age, layer activity, and per-model footprint, and integrating batch-aware compacting during low-latency windows. Deliverables: per-model memory curves, recommended allocator profiles (slab/span sizes, free-list thresholds), KV eviction policy defaults, batching knobs that trade unit-cost for tail-latency, and a small runtime toggle to enable model-tailored profiles at rollout time. Rationale: Existing one-size-fits-all memory configs cause either high overcommit (wasted capacity) or frequent OOMs for long-context workloads. By calibrating per-model profiles, Dedicated and Hosted runtimes can more reliably pack long-context sessions and reduce hardware waste. Risks and trade-offs: more aggressive eviction/compaction saves memory but can increase per-request latency (KV reloads) and marginally affect generation continuity; quantized kernels change footprint/fragmentation characteristics so profiles must be validated per quantization scheme. We will run quality regression evals and latency SLO checks before rollout.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Triage: scoped to Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B-Instruct and Qwen-14B both 32k and 64k contexts. Agreed to include both FP16 and 4-bit quantized variants in profiling.
2025-02-20 - Design sync with infra: Marcus proposed KV-slice size default of 512 tokens for 64k configs. Noted potential interaction with continuous batching kernel windows.

2025-02-25 - Initial profiling run on staging: observed 18% average peak memory reduction using aggressive slab compaction but 9% regression in 95p token latency for 32k streams. Logged artifacts and heatmaps: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/model-memory-heatmaps-83421
2025-02-27 - Trade-off decision: relax compaction aggressiveness for hosted tier; keep aggressive baseline for Dedicated experimental pool. Added rollout plan: dark-launch Dedicated first.

2025-03-01 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1789 implementing KV-slice residency table and allocator tuning flags. Benchmarks attached to PR: reduced peak GPU by 14% on Qwen-14B-64k (FP16), no quality regression on eval set alpha-ml-longctx-v2.

2025-03-03 - Code review feedback from Priya Rao: request explicit unit-tests for eviction ordering and a calibration script to auto-generate recommended slab sizes per model variant. Added task to follow-up.

2025-03-04 - Experiment update: tuned slice aging threshold from 12s to 6s for mixed-batch traffic; this recovered 95p latency to within 3% of baseline with 12% memory savings on average. Preparing benchmark dashboard to share with PMs.
acceptance_criteria: Per-model memory profile artifacts (CSV + visualization) for the three target models and both quantization schemes
Peak GPU residency reduced by >=12% for at least two of the three models at 64k context without >10% increase in 95p token latency
No sample-quality regressions on the long-context eval suite (alpha-ml-longctx-v2) beyond predefined thresholds
Allocator and KV defaults exposed as runtime flags and an automatic recommendation generator script
Rollout playbook documented with dark-launch and canary steps plus rollback criteria
